title: Justification
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Justification is God’s gracious act of declaring sinners righteous through faith in Jesus Christ. It is not based on human works, personal worthiness, or religious performance, but on the righteousness of Christ received by faith.
summary: Justification is God’s gracious act of declaring sinners righteous through faith in Jesus Christ. It is not based on human works, personal worthiness, or religious performance, but on the righteousness of Christ received by faith.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the righteousness of His people. Through His obedient life, atoning death, and resurrection, sinners who trust in Him are forgiven, counted righteous, and brought into peace with God.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Justification answers the question of how guilty sinners can stand before a holy God. Scripture teaches that all have sinned and fall short of God’s glory. No one can be justified by works of the law, personal obedience, moral effort, religious identity, or comparison with others.

God justifies sinners by grace through faith in Jesus Christ. This does not mean God pretends sin does not matter. At the cross, Christ bore sin and satisfied justice so that God may be both just and the justifier of the one who has faith in Jesus.

Justification includes forgiveness, but it is more than forgiveness. God not only pardons guilt; He declares the believer righteous in Christ. The sinner’s standing before God rests on Christ’s righteousness, not on fluctuating feelings, spiritual progress, or personal record.

Because justification is received by faith apart from works, boasting is excluded. The believer has peace with God not because he has earned acceptance, but because Christ has accomplished salvation and God has declared him righteous in Him.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many people live under the exhausting burden of trying to prove they are acceptable to God. They measure their standing by performance, emotions, ministry activity, recovery progress, or failure. Justification gives the believer a firmer foundation: peace with God rests on Christ, not on self.

This doctrine is also essential for the guilty and ashamed. The Gospel does not say, “Try harder until God accepts you.” It says that sinners are justified by grace through faith because Christ has done what they could never do. This truth humbles pride and comforts the broken.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Stand before God by faith in Christ, not by your own record. When guilt accuses you, return to the righteousness of Jesus. When pride rises, remember that you were justified by grace. Let justification produce humility, assurance, worship, repentance, and freedom to obey God from gratitude rather than fear.
